title: Gentle tone bridges and compact type scale for dense grids
creator: Maya Alvarez
description: Goal: introduce a small set of ‘tone bridge’ color steps and a condensed type scale to improve legibility and visual hierarchy in high-density data surfaces (tables, compact cards, and action rows) while preserving accessibility across light/dark modes. This ticket scopes the token definitions, sample component updates, migration guidance for product teams, and a lightweight QA checklist. Background: current tokens create visual clutter at small sizes; product teams report loss of contrast between rows and controls in dense states. We need a conservative change set that reduces token variance, simplifies radius/spacing options for compact components, and flattens shadow elevation at small z-depths to avoid visual noise on low-contrast surfaces.
acceptance_criteria: Define 3 new semantic tone-bridges per mode (light/dark) mapped to existing semantics (surface, elevated, hover)
Provide a 4-step condensed type scale (compact-xxxx to compact-sm) with numeric font-size and line-height tokens
Create spacing/radius presets for compact components: compact-gap, compact-padding, compact-radius
Reduce small-surface shadow/elevation to two micro-elevations and document when to use each
Figma file updated with token examples and component overrides; product teams sign-off on visual samples
Migration notes and a small codemod proposal drafted for front-end to rename legacy compact tokens
design_notes: Principles: 1) Conservative — maintain existing major semantics, introduce bridges only where they reduce ambiguity; 2) Scalable — tokens must extend to future density modes without proliferation; 3) Measurable — tie token changes to perceptual metrics (contrast ratio targets and visual weight tests). Tone-bridges are lower-contrast intermediates (approx contrast delta 0.08–0.12 relative to base surface) to avoid stepping the visual rhythm too aggressively. Compact type scale reduces font-size deltas and tightens line-height to maintain legibility at small line lengths. Radius choices favor 6px/4px for compact vs 8px/12px for default, but include a documented opt-in for brand-specific radii.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (Design): finalize token names and mapping table, publish token spec in Confluence and Figma
Phase 2 (Platform): add tokens to style token file and feature-flag the compact tokens behind 'compact_token_rollout'
Phase 3 (Components): ship component-level overrides for TableRow, ActionRow, CompactCard with token names and opt-in props
Phase 4 (Rollout): enable flag for internal apps, gather metrics for visual regressions and accessibility; then gradual public rollout
Phase 5 (Clean-up): propose codemod to rename legacy tokens and remove alias shim after 2 releases
notes_on_tradeoffs:
- Accessibility vs density: to keep contrast for critical text we keep body font weight at 400–500 for compact scale. Some product areas will need slightly larger sizes; add per-component opt-outs.
- Token surface granularity: fewer steps reduces flexibility but simplifies decisions for engineers. We prioritize 3 semantic steps to balance density and expressiveness.
- Shadows: flattening micro-shadow reduces perceived depth but improves focus in data-heavy UIs; we'll keep a single stronger elevation for modals and floating overlays.
